package.name: pimesh_core
package.description:
The three helpers more than one stage needs: a single-slot mailbox, a cv::Mat header laid over a ROS image without copying it, and the percentile and hash every probe reports its numbers through.
It exists because they were already crossing a package boundary. Before #14's P2 they lived in pimesh_perception, and pimesh_world — which has nothing else to do with perception — included all three of them: a mapping package depending on a perception one for a percentile. Splitting depth out of perception would have made that three consumers across three boundaries, so the question "do these have a home of their own" stopped being a preference and got answered by the include graph.
Header-only on purpose. There is no library target here, only headers and their tests: nothing in it needs linking, and a package that cannot fail to link is one fewer thing for the two distros to disagree about.
pimesh_camera keeps its own copy of the percentile and the hash rather than depending on this. That is deliberate and written down in its header: the Pi's package pointing at a dev-box one would be an edge running the wrong way down the pipeline for the sake of twelve lines.
